title: Agentic Postgres Reality Ledger
description: One row per product concept, saying what it is TODAY (ADR 0247). This schema is the shape; the guard in tests/contract/test_reality_ledger.py is the meaning: whether a row's evidence resolves, whether a row that is not reachable carries a control, and whether a customer sentence uses a word the release may not use. A file that validates here may still be refused there, because what a claim name resolves to depends on the newest evidence document and no schema can carry that.

rows.description: The concepts, in the order the page renders them. Ids are unique; the guard checks it, because a schema cannot compare one property across items.

id.description: A stable snake_case name. A console control and an /api/v1 operation type name the row they act on by this id (Sessions 37 and 42).

concept.description: The concept as a customer would name it.

status.description: `not_offered` is ADR 0247's addition: a concept cut by decision, which `planned` would promise.

customer_text.description: The sentence a customer reads about the concept. The only text in the ledger the forbidden-word guard reads.

today.description: What the appliance does now, for its operator.

today_evidence.description: A claim in evidence_claims.CLAIMS that passed in the newest evidence document, or a capacity.ENVELOPE subject, proving `today`; null when nothing does (D2009).

evidence.description: For an `available` or `beta` row, the claims or envelope subjects proving the customer-facing status; empty for every other status (D2009).

stage5_reality.description: What Stage 5 builds of it, or why it does not.

eventual.description: What a fuller product would do. Never promised.

controls.description: The console controls and /api/v1 operation types that act on the concept; empty until a session builds one.

since_session.description: The session the row's current status was set in.

target_session.description: The Stage 5 session that builds it, or null when no Stage 5 session does.
